subtitle: A balanced verdict: everything from this book in one debate
words.intro: Germany has a butcher in every village, and a government report on meat. At a family table, on a Sunday, with a roast, those two facts come together. Everybody has read a study.

grammar[0].blocks[2].text: German teachers mark down a discussion that ends in *es gibt Vor- und Nachteile*. Everybody knows that. Say which ones win, and why.
grammar[0].fact: Every German schoolchild writes an *Erörterung*, in which you’re expected to weigh up both sides before you conclude. So nearly everyone in the country can produce, in a pub or at a funeral, a paragraph that begins with *einerseits*.

grammar[1].blocks[1].text: Many Germans are unwilling to discuss money or how they vote at table. They’ll happily discuss a study, in detail, with the vegetables going cold. Now you can take part.
grammar[1].fact: *Der Klügere gibt nach*, the wiser one gives in, is what German grandparents say at the end of an argument, usually about themselves. It’s what you’ve learned in this chapter, with one small addition: *dennoch*.

document.intro: A real flyer on a street post in Wiesbaden, with tear-off strips. It offers a self-help group for people who feel guilty. It’s very serious. It’s also a joke. Read it and say which, and how you know. *Vielflieger*, *Fleischesser*, *Dieselfahrer*: there’s the debate in three words.
document.fact: Swedish gave the world *flygskam*, and German quickly had its own: *Flugscham*, flight shame. The star in *Vielflieger*in* is the German way of including all genders, and it’s a whole other Sunday lunch.

reading.intro: Sunday lunch at Lena’s aunt’s in the Eifel. Lena’s nephew, Tim, is sixteen and has just announced that he is a vegan. There’s a very large roast on the table. Frau Huber, who’s a guest, sits between him and his grandfather, and carries on eating.
reading.fact: Germans eat less meat than they did a generation ago. In 2013 a political party proposed a *Veggie Day* in public canteens, once a week. It was so unpopular that it is widely believed to have cost them votes.
